note: One record is made per state from each template. {state}, {slug} and {snap_slug} are filled in by scripts/lib.py. Edit this file, not the built pages.

templates.name: SNAP in {state}
templates.org: {state} SNAP agency, as listed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture
templates.what: SNAP helps households with low income buy groceries. This page links to {state}'s SNAP website and phone number and tells you how to apply.
templates.how: Open the {state} entry, then apply online or call the number it lists.

templates.name: WIC in {state}
templates.org: {state} WIC agency, through the U.S. Department of Agriculture
templates.what: Healthy foods, nutrition advice and breastfeeding support at no cost for women who are pregnant, recently pregnant or breastfeeding, and for babies and children under 5.
templates.how: On the apply page, choose {state} (or your Tribe) from the list. Then call or apply online with a WIC agency near you.

templates.name: Help with energy bills in {state}
templates.org: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)
templates.what: LIHEAP can help pay a share of heating and cooling bills. Each state runs its own program. Applying never costs a fee.
templates.how: Call the National Energy Assistance Referral line, weekdays 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. Eastern, and give your city, county and {state}.

templates.name: Dial 211 in {state}
templates.what: A free line that connects you to local help with housing, food, utilities, child care and more.
templates.how: Dial 211, or search by ZIP code at 211.org. Say what you need and your county.

templates.name: Health coverage for your child in {state}
templates.org: Insure Kids Now, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
templates.what: Medicaid and the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) cover many children in families with low or moderate income. {state} sets its own rules.
templates.how: Open the coverage page, choose {state}, and follow the steps to apply.

templates.name: Low-cost prenatal care near you in {state}
templates.org: HRSA health centers, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
templates.what: Health centers charge on a sliding fee scale, so you can get care even if you are uninsured or cannot pay.
templates.how: Search by ZIP code, call the center, and ask whether it provides prenatal care and what the sliding fee would be. Or call 1-800-311-BABY to find your area health department.

templates.name: Free diapers in {state}
templates.org: National Diaper Bank Network member banks
templates.what: The national directory lists member diaper banks by state and city.
templates.how: Find {state} in the directory and contact the bank nearest you to ask how to sign up. If none is close, dial 211 and ask about diaper help.

templates.name: Child care, child support and family help in {state}
templates.org: ChildCare.gov, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
templates.what: The {state} page gathers links for finding licensed child care, help paying for it, child support, health coverage and more.
templates.how: Open the {state} page and use its link to find child care near you.

templates.name: Head Start near you in {state}
templates.org: Office of Head Start, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
templates.what: Free learning and development for children from birth to age 5 in eligible families. All programs welcome children with disabilities.
templates.how: Enter your city or ZIP code in the locator, then call the program listed and ask how to enroll.

templates.name: Free legal help in {state}
templates.org: LawHelp.org and the Legal Services Corporation
templates.what: Legal aid offices help people with low income with custody, divorce, housing and benefits at no cost. Who qualifies depends on the office.
templates.how: Use LawHelp.org to choose {state} and find guides, forms and local contacts.

templates.name: Domestic violence help in {state}
templates.org: National Network to End Domestic Violence (NNEDV)
templates.what: {state} has a domestic violence coalition that knows the local shelters and programs. Shelter addresses are kept private for safety, so this site never lists them.
templates.how: Call the National Domestic Violence Hotline any hour, or open the list and choose your state's coalition.
